title: Jamaican Curry Goat with Rice and Peas
summary: Goat is marinated overnight in a homemade curry powder, then braised low and slow with potatoes until tender, served alongside coconut rice and peas.
equipment: large heavy casserole (Dutch oven, 6 litres) with lid
spice grinder or pestle and mortar

ingredients.item: boneless goat shoulder or leg, cut into 4 cm pieces
Scotch bonnet chilli, seeded and finely chopped
ingredients.note: wear gloves; use half for milder

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
floury potatoes, peeled, cut into 3 cm chunks
x 400 g tin red kidney beans, drained and rinsed
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make the curry powder
steps.text: Toast the cumin and fenugreek seeds in a dry frying pan over low heat for 2 minutes until fragrant, then grind them finely and mix with the ground coriander, turmeric, allspice and black pepper. Toasting whole seeds before grinding brings out far more aroma than using pre-ground spice straight from the jar.

steps.title: Marinate the goat
steps.text: In a large bowl, mix the goat with the onion, garlic, ginger, Scotch bonnet, spring onions, thyme, salt and half the curry powder. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight, since goat is a dense meat and needs a long soak in the seasoning to flavour it right through.

steps.title: Brown the goat
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large casserole over medium-high heat and stir in the remaining curry powder for 30 seconds to cook out its raw edge. Add the goat with all its marinade and stir for 8-10 minutes until the meat has coloured on all sides.

steps.title: Simmer until tender
steps.text: Pour in the water, scraping up any browned bits from the base of the pot, bring to the boil, then cover and simmer gently for 1 hour 30 minutes, stirring every 20 minutes. Add the potatoes and continue simmering, partly covered, for 45 minutes to 1 hour, until the goat is tender and some of the potato has broken down to thicken the sauce.

steps.title: Cook the rice and peas
steps.text: About 30 minutes before the curry is ready, put the kidney beans, coconut milk, water, spring onions, thyme and allspice berries in a saucepan with the rice salt, bring to the boil, then stir in the rice. Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 18-20 minutes until the liquid is absorbed, then rest for 5 minutes off the heat before removing the spring onions and thyme and fluffing with a fork. The tight-fitting lid traps the steam so the rice cooks evenly without needing to be stirred.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon the curry goat into bowls alongside the rice and peas. The coconut rice is mild enough to balance the heat and spice of the curry.

tips: Marinating the goat overnight makes a noticeable difference, since this cut benefits from a long soak in the seasoning.
A common mistake is rushing the simmer; goat needs a full 1 hour 30 minutes or more of gentle cooking to become tender, so resist turning up the heat.
Toast the cumin and fenugreek seeds before grinding; it makes the homemade curry powder far more fragrant.
Keep the rice pan's lid on tightly while it cooks so the liquid doesn't escape before the rice has absorbed it.
Letting some potato break down naturally thickens the curry without needing any extra flour.
safety: Wear gloves when handling the Scotch bonnet and avoid touching your face.
storage: Cool leftovers within 2 hours, refrigerate for up to 3 days, and reheat until piping hot (74°C) throughout before serving; the rice and peas can be stored and reheated the same way.
